items.text: As seen from your current location, when will an upright flagpole cast no shadow because the Sun is directly above the flagpole?

options.label: B
options.text: Only on the first day of summer.

options.label: C
options.text: Only on the first day of winter.

options.label: D
options.text: On both the first days of spring and fall.

items.text: When the Moon appears to completely cover the Sun (an eclipse), the Moon must be at which phase?

Imagine you are building a scale model of the Earth and the Moon using a 12-inch basketball for the Earth and a 3-inch tennis ball for the Moon. To maintain the proper distance scale, about how far from the surface of the basketball should the tennis ball be placed?

You have two balls of equal size and smoothness (ignore air resistance), one heavy and one much lighter. You hold one in each hand at the same height and release them at the same time. What will happen?

options.label: A
options.text: The heavier one will hit the ground first.

options.label: B
options.text: They will hit the ground at the same time.

options.label: C
options.text: The lighter one will hit the ground first.

items.text: How does the speed of radio waves compare to the speed of visible light?

options.label: B
options.text: They both travel at the same speed.

items.text: Astronauts inside the Space Shuttle float around as it orbits the Earth because

options.label: A
options.text: there is no gravity in space.

options.label: B
options.text: they are falling in the same way as the Space Shuttle.

options.label: C
options.text: they are above the Earth's atmosphere.

options.label: D
options.text: there is less gravity inside the Space Shuttle.

options.label: E
options.text: more than one of the above.

items.text: Imagine the Earth's orbit were changed to be a perfect circle about the Sun so that the distance to the Sun never changed. How would this affect the seasons?

options.label: A
options.text: We would no longer experience a difference between the seasons.

options.label: B
options.text: We would still experience seasons, but the difference would be much LESS noticeable.

options.label: C
options.text: We would still experience seasons, but the difference would be much MORE noticeable.

options.label: D
options.text: We would continue to experience seasons in the same way we do now.

items.text: Where does the Sun's energy come from?

options.label: A
options.text: The combining of light elements into heavier elements

options.label: B
options.text: The breaking apart of heavy elements into lighter ones

options.label: D
options.text: Heat left over from the Big Bang

items.text: On about September 22, the Sun sets directly to the west (as shown on the diagram). Where would the Sun appear to set two weeks later?

If you could see stars during the day, the sky at noon shows the Sun near the constellation Gemini. Near which constellation would you expect the Sun to be located at sunset? (constellations shown east→west: Leo, Cancer, Gemini, Taurus, Pisces)
Compared to the distance to the Moon, how far away is the Space Shuttle (when in space) from the Earth?

options.label: B
options.text: About half way to the Moon

options.label: D
options.text: About twice as far as the Moon

items.text: The stars of the Big Dipper form the shape of a pot with a curved handle. To where would you have to travel to first observe a considerable change in that shape?
Which list is correctly arranged in order of closest-to-most-distant from the Earth?
Which of the following would make you weigh half as much as you do right now?

options.label: A
options.text: Take away half of the Earth's atmosphere.

options.label: B
options.text: Double the distance between the Sun and the Earth.

options.label: C
options.text: Make the Earth spin half as fast.

options.label: D
options.text: Take away half of the Earth's mass.

options.label: E
options.text: More than one of the above

items.text: A person reads a newspaper standing 5 feet from a table with an unshaded 100-watt bulb. If the table were moved to 10 feet, how many bulbs in total would be needed to light the newspaper to the same brightness as before?
According to modern ideas and observations, what can be said about the location of the center of the Universe?

options.label: A
options.text: The Earth is at the center.

options.label: B
options.text: The Sun is at the center.

options.label: C
options.text: The Milky Way Galaxy is at the center.

options.label: D
options.text: An unknown, distant galaxy is at the center.

options.label: E
options.text: The Universe does not have a center.
